summary.text: William Lawrence, a Democratic climate and housing organizer, won the election for Michigan's 7th District on November 3, 2026, defeating Republican incumbent Rep. Tom Barrett, and is set to take office on January 3, 2027.
He co-founded the Sunrise Movement and later helped found tenant-organizing groups in mid-Michigan, and the race was his first run for office.

paragraphs.text: William Lawrence was born in 1990 in Madison, Wisconsin, and moved to East Lansing at age five, according to Wikipedia. He graduated from East Lansing High School, and his campaign website also says he was raised in East Lansing.
He earned a bachelor's degree in sociology and anthropology from Swarthmore College, per Wikipedia.

In 2015 Lawrence co-founded the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization. He worked there as development director and later as director of strategic partnerships before leaving in 2020, per Wikipedia.

Since 2020 he has worked on housing issues in Michigan, founding the Mid-Michigan Tenant Resource Center and helping found the Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High Coalition, which his campaign website says has won statewide protections for low-income renters.

Lawrence won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for Michigan's 7th District, defeating Bridget Brink and Matt Maasdam, in his first run for Congress. He faced Republican incumbent Rep. Tom Barrett in the November general election.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife live in Lansing.
According to his campaign website, he campaigned on housing affordability, Medicare for All and climate action.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 51.0% of the vote to Tom Barrett's 47.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
